Western Heat Dome: 2026-03-21 -- The Crest

What Happened
The heat dome reached its maximum geographic extent. At least 14 states broke their all-time March temperature records between Thursday and Saturday: California, Arizona, Nevada, Utah, Wyoming, Idaho, Colorado, New Mexico, Kansas, Nebraska, Iowa, South Dakota, Minnesota, and Missouri. Kansas hit 101F at Phillipsburg. Iowa reached 97F at Hitchcock -- smashing a record from 1986 by 5 degrees. At Chanute KS, temperatures swung from a record low of 13F on March 16 to a record high of 91F four days later -- a 78F swing. The NCEI registered 479 stations breaking March records from Wednesday through Saturday; the true count is likely higher.

Climate Attribution
Climate Shift Index: Level 5 (maximum). WWA confirmed the event as "virtually impossible" without human-induced climate change and 800 times more likely due to fossil fuel burning. The anthropogenic signal added at least 4.7F (2.6C) to the heat. CSI 5 conditions now cover an area from the Pacific Coast to the Mississippi River -- roughly 1,800 miles of continuous extreme anomaly.

Earth System Context
Climate Change: The simultaneous record-breaking across 14 states is the signature of a shifted climate baseline. These are not daily records (which break regularly) but all-time monthly records -- the kind that stand for decades. Many of the previous records dated to 1907 and survived 119 years. They fell in a single weekend. The anomalies in the Plains (37-45F above normal) exceed even the Western core values, because the Plains in late March normally sit near 50-60F -- the gap between normal and midsummer is enormous.

Freshwater Change: Colorado snowpack stands at 40% of median -- the lowest for this date in 41 years of records. The expansion into the Front Range accelerates a snowpack crisis already underway from the warmest winter on record. The Arkansas, Platte, and Colorado River headwaters are all in the anomaly zone. Rapid melt overwhelms reservoirs and the water that runs off in March is unavailable in August when demand peaks.

Biosphere Integrity: The Great Plains expansion brings the heat dome directly over the winter wheat belt. Winter wheat vernalizes (completes its cold requirement) in March. Sudden heat forces premature heading, reducing grain fill and yield. The US winter wheat crop across Kansas, Oklahoma, and Texas provides ~25% of US wheat production. Heat stress during vernalization is one of the highest-impact climate risks to global grain supply. The Chanute KS temperature swing (78F in four days) exemplifies the whiplash that stresses both natural and agricultural systems.

Land System Change: Fire preconditioning now extends from California chaparral to Great Plains rangeland. NWS issued red flag warnings across Nebraska, Kansas, and Oklahoma. The Morrill County fire in western Nebraska is already the state's largest on record. Prescribed burn windows are eliminated when conditions jump straight from winter to fire weather.

Data & Sources
Temperature data: ERA5 reanalysis via CDS API when available; synthetic grid seeded with confirmed NWS records as fallback.
Attribution: World Weather Attribution rapid analysis (800x more likely, +4.7F/2.6C); Climate Central Climate Shift Index.
Planetary boundaries: Rockstrom et al. (2009), Richardson et al. (2023).
